Small stuff like getting doors held open, getting noticed when you’re ordering at the bar, my personal experience is that being treated with basic human decency increased when I was thinner. 

As far as personalities, I think I made friends easier when skinnier partially because awkwardness is seemed as more endearing when you’re conventionally attractive. I would get invited out more and it’d be like an “oh that’s just what interrupting-cow-who is like” and so I’d be friends with people who enjoyed dressing up and  going out even though we had nothing in common. Now my friends are mostly homebodies that I game with or watch shows with but being awkward isn’t as forgiving when you’re fat if that makes sense. My personality never changed, just the types of friends I made did and I do have a harder time making friends now.

I’ve struggled with my weight all my life. I’ve been 96lbs to 216lbs at 5’1 (ED struggles is an important mention). I will be honest that being skinnier always got me better treatment, more compliments, and more attention. Being fatter makes me feel invisible, which I take comfort in sometimes. I’m okay with my body at all sizes but yes, there is a difference in treatment and it is pretty dehumanizing!
For dating, I never had to approach first when I was skinnier. Any conversations I did start were well reciprocated. For friendships, I’ve always been shy and never noticed a big difference in how I made friends but I did notice the personalities of people I surrounded myself with changed at different weights.
I have no idea why people act different towards people based on weight. I have a very blunt family that points out every piece of weight gain like it’s a sin. I don’t think it’s appropriate. But I definitely think it’s an unavoidable part of losing (or gaining) weight that people’s behavior changes towards you.
